reason: Both use the same sound banner structure: the headline dominates, the CTA sits at bottom left and the legal text sits beside it. In both, the Solstice can is shrunk so far that its label can't be read and it reads as a minor corner graphic rather than the hero, and the legal text is tiny and wraps to four lines. A turns the light-blue circle into a backdrop for the GLACIER logo, which is odd but tidy. In B, the light-blue circle is cropped at the bottom-right edge and cuts through the legal text, an unintended overlap, so A is slightly cleaner.

A: the orange divider runs straight through the body copy, striking out 'seaside kitchen', which is a clear unwanted collision. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has been moved from above the headline to a tiny, illegible spot beside the CTA, and the headline is jammed right under the logo bar. B: no collisions, but its problems are close to A's: the eyebrow is again tiny and misplaced at the bottom, the headline is jammed against the logo bar and pressed to the side edges, the divider is crammed under the headline, and the logo bar now sits inset with a dark border instead of running full width. B wins only because it avoids A's strike-through collision.

A keeps the original's centred top-to-bottom stack, but the legal line is blown up to near-body size and wedged tight between the headline and the CTA. That breaks the reading order and crowds the button, and 'of' is left dangling at the end of the headline's first line. B breaks the composition apart: the sale banner floats mid-left on top of a decorative circle, away from the product, and the product is pushed off to the right. The left-aligned CTA no longer lines up with the centred headline, and the oversized legal block beside the CTA competes with it for attention.

Both reflow the headline into the same five-line stack with awkward breaks ('and a' / 'little' left as near-orphans) and the headline runs almost to the side edges. A's 'Now in four flavours' subline is shrunk to small, hard-to-read text and floats in a large dead gap below the headline. B keeps the subline and CTA at legible sizes, but its pill is almost full-width and crowds the bottom edge with a tight margin. B is slightly better because its secondary copy stays readable.

The two are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The headline has grown huge and now crowds an oversized CTA pill. The supporting tagline has been pushed to the top right, small and above the button, which breaks the reading order. The three flavour chips are shrunk, run in reverse order and sit jammed under the button against the headline's descender line. The left column is a cramped block with no breathing room. The only difference is that B's CTA pill is a few pixels wider and sits closer to the right edge, and that is not enough to separate them.

Both candidates look the same. In each, the NEW badge has shrunk to an illegible pill, and the product can is a tiny thumbnail jammed between the badge and the Try It button, which crowds into the can from below. The supporting copy breaks into a cramped three-line block ending on the orphan 'now.', and the right-hand cluster is crowded while the headline sits alone on the left, so the layout reads as scattered fragments rather than an intentional banner. Neither has a visible flaw the other lacks.

A keeps 'Sunset Sessions' as the clear dominant headline on one line, but 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' now sits below the headline, so the reading order is inverted. The subtitle and date blocks are cramped mid-banner, the RSVP button is no bigger than the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills so the CTA doesn't stand out, the legal text is microscopic, and the missing-asset placeholder is still visible. B is worse: the headline breaks onto two lines and loses scale, and 'Saturday 21 June' competes with it. The italic subtitle is squeezed into an illegible 7-line sliver, the eyebrow and logo are crammed into the top-left over the brown circle, and B has the same overloaded right cluster with an undifferentiated CTA, tiny legal text and the placeholder box.

A and B are almost identical, and both have the same serious flaws. The RSVP Free CTA has shrunk to a small pill with tiny text and sits in a row of four, smaller than the FREE ENTRY, ALL AGES and TASTINGS tags, so the call to action is buried. The 'Solstice Presents' kicker is detached under the logo, the left column of logo, tagline and can is cramped against the large title block, and the canvas is busier than the original. The only differences are that B has a slightly larger date, a wider ALL AGES pill and a slightly larger URL line. None of these changes the verdict.

Both are the same sound left-to-right banner, but both share the same flaws: the '48H ONLY' badge has shrunk to an unreadable dot, and the VOLTSTRIDE box is jammed against the bottom-left edge. In A the body copy has a little more room between it and the CTA. In B the body copy nearly touches the 'Shop the Archive' button and the box crowds the green panel's edge, so B looks slightly more cramped.

A: the can has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed against the top edge, with the sun almost clipped and the SOLSTICE label unreadable. Its legal copy sits on the bottom-right decorative circle and is about 7px tall, and the hero product is now weaker than the logo. B: the logo sits inside a light-blue circle that is cut off at the canvas edge, and two circles compete across the top. Its can is also small with an illegible label and its legal text is still tiny, but the legal sits on a clean background and the top band looks more balanced. B is the less bad of the two.

A keeps a sensible left-to-right order (presenter, headline, date, can, CTA), but it is badly fragmented. The tagline is squeezed into a 6-line sliver column, the RSVP pill is the same size as the info pills so the CTA gets lost, the can is a tiny afterthought and the legal block is nearly as prominent as the details. B has the stronger one-line headline, but 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits under the title, which inverts the reading order. B's tagline and the 'Reserve a spot' line are jammed against the top edge, 'Saturday 21 June' breaks awkwardly beside a cramped 3-line detail block, the pills form a ragged 2x2 with uneven gaps and the logo wordmark looks clipped. Overall B is more cramped and disordered than A.

A and B are essentially the same image; B only moves the CTA and legal text down by about 2px. Both share the same flaws: the headline is oversized and swamps everything, and the bottle is small and stuck in the upper left, leaving a large empty band in the middle. The offer copy is squeezed into a narrow right column with ragged breaks, the CTA is small and buried, and the legal fine print is set as large as the offer copy, so the hierarchy is broken.

A: the banner reads left to right sensibly, but the headline's final period almost touches the right column. The subline is squeezed into a narrow 4-line centred rag ('Now in four / flavours.'), and the CTA sits close to the right and bottom edges. B has the same structure but worse: the subline breaks into 5 cramped lines ('Solstice / botanical…') that start near the top edge and nearly touch the CTA pill, so the right column looks jammed and lopsided against the headline.

A: the subhead is squeezed into a narrow 3-line column next to the CTA, and the flavour pills are scattered out of their original order (Honey Rosemary left, Cucumber Mint far right, Blood Orange stranded below), so the row no longer reads as one group. B has the same scattered pills, and its subhead is worse: crushed into a 4-line column of tiny text that butts against an oversized CTA slab, which competes with the headline. B's peach circle is also shrunk to a stray fragment in the corner, so B is the weaker of the two.

The two are almost identical. Both crowd the 'Sunset Sessions' headline against the edge of the circle. Both put the RSVP button in the same grid as the Free Entry, All Ages and Tastings pills, so the CTA reads as just another tag. Both strand 'Reserve a spot' on the right, away from its button, cram the fine print to an unreadable size, and clip the placeholder image at the bottom edge. A's 'Saturday 21 June' is larger and competes with the headline, so B's slightly smaller date keeps a marginally clearer hierarchy.

A and B look identical: the quote and attribution are moved neatly to the left with the big quote mark, and the can-in-circle sits on the right. Both have the same flaws. The logo strip floats on its own in the middle gap, cut off from the brand content and competing for attention between the quote and the product. The SOLSTICE label on the shrunken can can't be read. The circle is squeezed against the top and bottom edges, so the right side feels cramped next to the roomy quote block.

A blows the 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM' attribution up to a bold lime block that outweighs the quote, so the hierarchy is inverted. The quote shrinks to small text with ragged breaks ('bright, a / little bitter'). The purple circle is moved to the top corner behind the quote mark and no longer frames the can, which is small. B keeps the quote as the clear dominant element at a readable size, but it moves the attribution above the quote as tiny text, which breaks the reading order and leaves it hard to read. B's circle is also detached from the can at the top, and its short lines ('Like a', 'soon.') wrap raggedly. B has the better hierarchy and is fixable; A is broken.

The two are almost pixel-identical. B's attribution is set very slightly wider, and that's the only difference. Both share the same flaws. The quote mark is stranded at the top-left, with a large dead gap above the quote. The quote and the 'ULTRA TASTING TEAM' credit are pushed down near the bottom edge with little margin. The logo has moved off its left-margin anchor into the purple circle under the can, where it reads as a stray product caption. The 'SOLSTICE' label on the can is tiny.

Both rebuild the design sensibly as a skyscraper: stripe band up top, lime panel, stacked headline, CTA at the bottom. Both shrink the VOLTSTRIDE box to a small afterthought that straddles the stripe/lime seam, and both let the oversized 48H ONLY badge compete with the product. A spaces the badge and box apart more evenly, but its body copy runs almost to the side edges and nearly matches the headline in weight. In B the box is jammed right under a badge that dominates the stripe band, though B's smaller body copy has better margins. A is marginally the better resize.

A keeps a clear hierarchy, with the headline dominant and the body text and CTA in one row, but the '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' eyebrow is tiny and sits apart under the logo instead of above the headline, and the fine print is too small to read. B blows the eyebrow up to near-headline weight with a bad '24 / READERS' line break, which competes with the headline; the body text is jammed between it and a CTA stranded far right, and the book cover butts against the card edge.

A: the 'Shop Flavours' CTA is oversized and competes with the headline. The subline is squeezed into a narrow column beside it with awkward breaks ('drinks, one / long season.'). The flavour pills are out of the original order and scattered across three positions, and the peach circle is cut down to a stray fragment in the corner. B: the subline wraps better, the CTA is better scaled, and the peach circle layers deliberately behind the CTA. However, the pills are still scattered and reordered, Blood Orange is noticeably larger than the other two, and Cucumber Mint sits on the circle while the rest of the copy is left-aligned, so the bottom half feels unplanned.

The two layouts are almost the same; the only difference is that B's 'Saturday 21 June' is slightly larger, which makes it compete more with the headline without fixing anything. Both share the same flaws: 1) The 'RSVP Free' CTA is shrunk to the size of the FREE ENTRY, ALL AGES and TASTINGS pills and placed in their grid, so it reads as a fourth tag. 2) Its 'Reserve a spot' URL line is stranded far right under the product. 3) 'Sessions' crowds the bottom-left edge. 4) The legal line is unreadably tiny, and a red placeholder box sits clipped at the bottom edge.

The two are almost identical. Both put the quote text low, leaving a large empty gap under the quote mark, and the attribution sits close to the bottom edge. The logo has moved off the left column into the purple circle under the product, so it reads as product decoration rather than branding. In A the attribution is set larger, wider than the quote block, and competes with the quote. B's attribution is slightly smaller and more subordinate, so B edges ahead.

Both candidates have the same broken structure. The CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill that is almost unreadable, the legal text is microscopic, and the dark header bar survives only as a stray dark block in the top-right corner. The logo has lost its header band, the orange divider has become a tiny stray dash at top left, and the right-hand body column is cramped against the edge while the headline crowds the middle. A is slightly worse: its body copy wraps into seven ragged lines in a very narrow column. B's six lines wrap more evenly, but its leftover dark block is larger and more distracting.

Both moved the orange divider above the headline and dropped the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow below it, shrunk to illegible micro-text. The legal block is also tiny in both. In A the body copy stays clearly below the headline in size and the CTA keeps comfortable side margins, but there is a large dead gap between the body copy and the button. In B the body copy is blown up nearly to headline weight, so the two compete. It breaks into a ragged 8-line column, and the CTA pill almost touches both canvas edges, which makes it look cramped and less intentional.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The product image is shrunk into a small top-right circle. The 'Find It Near You' CTA is a tiny pill set beside the badges instead of standing out, and it comes before the body copy, which sits stranded at the bottom right, so the reading order is broken. Elements are scattered in a two-column grid with large dead gaps, the 'Free Delivery' tag lands mid-canvas, and the 'BACKBY DEMAND' label loses its space. B differs only by sub-pixel shifts.

The two layouts are nearly identical. Both shrink the phone to a tiny icon jammed against the left edge, with its green circle backdrop reduced to a barely visible sliver. Both make the 'Back by demand' and 'Summer only' pills the same size as the 'Find It Near You' CTA, so the button gets lost among them, and both leave a large empty band above the headline. A is worse because its subhead is bigger than the CTA text and wraps into three ragged lines that compete with the headline. B's two-line subhead is properly subordinate.

A squeezes the subhead into a narrow four-line column ('sparkling / drinks, one') next to an oversized CTA pill that outweighs the headline. Its flavour chips are reordered and scattered in a zigzag, and the peach circle is shrunk to a corner fragment. B gives the subhead a wider three-line column and a more proportionate CTA, and it keeps the peach circle as a backdrop. But B's chips are still out of order and loosely spread, the Cucumber Mint chip floats alone on the circle, and the CTA's right edge isn't aligned with the headline.

The two are almost identical. Both put the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker hard against the top edge. Both set the body copy so large that it competes with the '20% off' headline. Both shrink the legal line to illegible micro-type, and both make the product a tiny cut-off can inside a cramped circle. B's slightly bigger 'Shop Sale' button leaves the legal text almost touching its bottom edge. A keeps a little more breathing room there, so it edges ahead by a hair.

Both use the same scattered layout. The 'Sunset Sessions' headline sits on the sun circle. The tagline is pushed into a narrow left column. RSVP is boxed into a right column next to the date. The FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills are stacked with large uneven gaps and pulled away from the event details. The bottom-left is mostly empty apart from the can. Reading order runs brand → tagline → date → CTA → pills, which is jumbled. B is worse because its time/location line is shrunk to tiny type that runs almost into the RSVP column. A keeps that line at a readable size with a clean two-line wrap.

A: the order reads left to right sensibly (logo, headline, tagline/date, product, CTA), but the four pills are stacked into a cramped vertical tower in which RSVP Free is just another tiny pill, and the missing partner-mark placeholder has been blown up into a prominent broken box on the right. B: the headline runs almost into the tagline column, 'Saturday 21 June' wraps awkwardly onto two lines jammed against the time copy, and the 2x2 pill grid plus the tiny body text make the middle cramped and hard to read; the placeholder is smaller but the layout is more crowded overall.

A: the headline is oversized and nearly touches the steps column (a gutter of about 15px between 'cup' and '03'). The CTA pill is huge and competes with the headline. The bag is shoved into the bottom-left corner against the canvas edge, the logo is shrunk to a dot, and the legal text is illegibly small. B has a cleaner two-column split with a real gutter. The bag sits on its circle as in the original, and the CTA is better proportioned. However, the headline wraps awkwardly with 'Three' alone on line one, the logo hangs left of the eyebrow/headline edge (43 vs 80px), the bag and step text are small, and the legal text is again microscopic.

Both use the same broken structure. The background photo has become an empty brown box that takes up about a third of the canvas, while the product bag is shrunk into a small tile. The logo is moved down beside the bag at the same weight instead of heading the layout. 'on' sits alone on its own line, and the body copy is cramped. B is almost identical, but its oversized SAVE 15% badge competes with the headline more than A's smaller badge does, so A is marginally less bad.

A keeps the headline dominant and a readable 'Enter Now' CTA, but the shoe is shrunk to a tiny icon crammed against the LIMITED badge and CTA in the top-right corner, and the body copy wraps into three cramped lines of near-illegible text. B is worse: the CTA and LIMITED badge are shrunk to unreadable specks under the shoe, so the call to action is effectively lost, and the body copy is jammed against the right edge with no margin.

Both use the same left-to-right banner structure. In both, the lime circle is clipped at the top and bottom edges of the canvas, the NEW VIDEO pill sits under the logo but is not aligned with it, and 'Full review inside.' is so small it is hard to read. A wraps that line onto two lines and jams it against the shoe. B keeps it on one line with cleaner spacing on the right, though its pill floats a little further from the logo. B is marginally the better of the two.

Both move the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow below the headline, which breaks the reading order, and shrink it to near-illegible microtype; both also squeeze the logo into a tiny bar and push the divider up above the headline. In A, the body copy is set almost as large as the headline, so it competes as a second focal point, and the CTA pill nearly touches both canvas edges. B keeps the body copy clearly smaller than the headline and gives the CTA proper side margins, so its hierarchy is cleaner.

A: the three flavour pills are out of their original order (Honey Rosemary first, Blood Orange alone on a second row) and scattered across two rows, Cucumber Mint sits on the peach circle, and the subhead wraps into a cramped 3-line column, but the headline still clearly leads and the CTA is sized sensibly. B: the Shop Flavours button is blown up until it competes with the headline, which squeezes the subhead into a 4-line sliver of tiny text with awkward breaks. Its pills are just as jumbled and spread out, and the peach circle is cut down to a stray fragment in the corner.

A: the dark header band stops at about x=575 and leaves a cream strip above it. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow right column with choppy one- and two-word lines, and its type is larger than the CTA's. The orange divider runs through the line 'gone until next', and the CTA label is tiny, which breaks both hierarchy and collision rules. B: the headline block is centred and well set, and the bottom row (body, CTA, ship date) reads left to right like a banner. But the SOLSTICE wordmark stays white on cream and is nearly invisible, so the brand is damaged. The dark band is cut down to a stray top-right fragment, the divider is orphaned near the logo, and 'Ships late June' competes with the CTA.

A: the left-headline, right-column banner layout works, but the narrow right column squeezes the subhead into 4 ragged centred lines ('Now in four / flavours.'). The headline also nearly touches that column, and the CTA sits close to the bottom edge. B: same structure, but the column is narrower still. The subhead breaks into 5 choppy lines and starts right at the top edge, and the CTA is nearly flush with the bottom, so the right column reads as cramped and unfinished.

Both are almost the same layout: the headline is big on the left, and 'Now in four flavours' sits in a narrow right column above a tiny CTA. In both, the 'See the Flavours' button has shrunk to near-unreadable text and is jammed against the period of 'sunshine.', and the two-line subcopy is squeezed into a cramped column. B's right column sits a few pixels closer to the headline's vertical centre, while A's subcopy rides slightly higher. The difference is too small to call a winner.

Both are nearly identical left-to-right leaderboards with a sensible headline, copy, product and CTA order. Both share the same flaws: 'WEEKEND ONLY' and the legal line under the button are microscopic and unreadable, and there is a dead gap between the body copy and the product. A centres the can neatly inside its peach circle, so the cluster looks deliberate. In B the smaller can sits off-centre against the circle's left edge, which looks accidental, and the button is slightly heavier.

The two layouts are almost the same. In both, 'Every mixed case.' is forced into a narrow three-line stack. The product is shrunk to a tiny tile on a purple disc, and its label can't be read. 'Ends Sunday. Online only.' is jammed about 4–5px from the disc's edge, with a dead empty strip on the right. 'WEEKEND ONLY' is so small it's hard to read. A leaves slightly more gap around the button and B is a few pixels tighter, but the difference doesn't matter.

A reads left to right in a sensible order (brand, big two-line headline, details column, can, CTA cluster). But the RSVP button is no bigger than the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills, so the CTA competes with them, the broken image placeholder overlaps the URL text, and the copy in the middle column is small and cramped. B breaks up the layout: the time/venue line is stranded on the far left away from its date, 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' is tiny and cut off from the headline and logo, RSVP is buried as just another pill in the row with a squeezed 'FREEENTRY', the URL sits top right away from the CTA, and the logo is jammed into the corner against the decorative circle.

Both share the same broken skeleton. The missing partner-mark placeholder is blown up to fill the right third, the RSVP CTA is shrunk to badge size and sits inline with the pills so it gets buried, and the legal copy is tiny. A also loses the Solstice sun icon and crams 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' tiny above the logo. B keeps the logo with its icon and uses a slightly smaller placeholder, but strands 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' on the far right, away from the headline.

Both demote the RSVP CTA to a tiny pill lost among the badges, blow the grey placeholder image up into the largest block on the right, and shrink the legal text to an illegible size, so neither has a clear hierarchy. A also wraps the italic tagline into a cramped four-line column and leaves 'June' orphaned on its own line. B keeps the tagline and 'Saturday 21 June' on one line each, but crushes '6 pm, Harbour Rooftop' into a narrow three-line stack jammed against the pills. B is slightly cleaner overall.

A splits the layout sensibly: the quote sits on the left and the can in its circle on the right. Its flaws are a large dead gap between the quote mark and the quote, a tiny can whose 'SOLSTICE' label can't be read, and a logo crammed in on the attribution's baseline at the right. B makes the quote bigger and more readable, but the text runs tight against the right edge. Its can is jammed against the bottom edge, and the logo floats at an arbitrary mid-right spot, so the bottom half looks scattered and unbalanced.

A: the Inkwell & Lantern logo straddles the card's top edge, so the lantern and 'INKWELL &' sit on the busy confetti. The '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' kicker floats in the right column, far from the headline it introduces. The headline is pushed to the bottom-left below a large empty area under the book, so the reading order is jumbled. B: no collisions, and the headline and CTA hierarchy is strong. But the card covers almost the whole canvas, so the confetti that defines the original's look is reduced to edge slivers. The kicker is moved below the logo, enlarged until it competes with the headline, and wraps awkwardly ('24 / READERS'). The legal line is crammed in tiny text beside the CTA.

The two are almost the same. Both make the headline huge and push it right up against the right column, so the period after 'sunshine.' nearly touches the CTA and the headline has very little margin at the top. Both shrink the 'See the Flavours' pill to a tiny button that is lost next to the headline. B's italic subline and button are slightly larger and easier to read than A's, which are cramped and small, so B is marginally less bad.
